1A.title: Why did they call you that?
words: the name your parents chose for you
My first name is quite unusual in this country.
We're on first-name terms with our boss.
She kept her own surname when she got married.
It's a very common surname here.
an informal name that friends or family use
a woman's surname before she married
The bank asked for my mother's maiden name.
the first letters of your names
He signs his emails with his initials.
be given the same name as somebody
I was named after my grandfather.
She was named after her aunt.
She changed her name when she became an actor.
He changed his name to Alex.
be a shorter form of a name
say a word or name correctly
People often can't pronounce my surname.
say or write the letters of a word
Could you spell your surname for me?
Some people think my name sounds old-fashioned.

g.title: Pronouns
g.rule:
English has several sets of pronouns. Choose by the job the word does in the sentence.

subject · objectShe called me. · They named him after his uncle.
possessive adjective · possessive pronounIt's my name. · The idea was mine.
reflexiveI introduced myself. · She taught herself.
two objectsThey gave her a nickname. · They gave it to her.

ex.q: My parents named ___ after my grandmother.
Is this pen yours or ___?
He introduced ___ to the class.

talk: How did your parents choose your name? Do you like it?
Which names are popular in your country now, and which sound old-fashioned?

lessons.title: Speaking: Why did they call you that?

1B.title: Life in colour
words: having a lot of bright colours
The market is full of colourful scarves.
He painted the door a bright red.
She chose a pale blue for the bedroom.
He wore a pale green shirt.
The office walls are a dull grey.
Yellow is a cheerful colour for a kitchen.
Some people find red rooms stressful.
Green has a calming effect on most people.
The music has a calming effect.
Black can look powerful in a business suit.
The paint is good quality and affordable.
Dark colours aren't suitable for a small room.
The film isn't suitable for children.
not strong or bright, like beige
We painted the hall in a neutral colour.

g.title: Adjectives
g.rule:
Three things to know about adjectives.

comparingBlue is more calming than red. · It's the brightest room in the house.
the + adjective = a groupThe young prefer bright colours.
one / onesI like the blue shirt, but I prefer the green one.
-ed and -ingI'm bored. · The colour is boring.

ex.q: This is ___ colour in the shop.
I don't like the grey jacket. Have you got a black ___?
Pale colours are ___ (relaxing) than bright ones.

talk: What is your favourite colour, and what does it make you feel?
Describe the colours of your home. Would you change any?

2A.title: Get ready! Get set! Go!
words: put things into a bag for a trip
I'm packing for my trip to Turkey.
a large bag for clothes when you travel
I can't lift this heavy suitcase.
bags you take onto the plane with you
I only take hand luggage on short trips.
You can take hand luggage for free.
a bag you carry on your back
He's travelling round Asia with a backpack.
an official document for travelling abroad
I always check that my passport is in my bag.
I need to renew my passport.
a device for charging a phone or laptop
I never remember to pack my charger.
a device for using a plug in another country
You need an adaptor for British sockets.
I bought a travel adaptor at the airport.
Put your toiletries in a clear plastic bag.
She packed a small bag of toiletries.
a box of things for small injuries
We always take a first-aid kit when we go camping.
Don't forget to take a first-aid kit.
a book with information for tourists
We're setting off at five in the morning.
He always packs at the last minute.
leave + noun + until the last minute
I leave everything until the last minute.

g.title: Present tenses
g.rule:
Choose between the present simple and the present continuous.

habits and facts → present simpleI usually pack the night before.
now or temporary → present continuousI'm packing my suitcase at the moment.
future arrangements → present continuousWe're flying on Friday.
timetables → present simpleThe train leaves at six.

ex.q: We ___ to Istanbul on Saturday. I've got the tickets.
The flight ___ at 7.45 every morning.
I never ___ (pack) at the last minute.

talk: How do you prepare for a trip? What do you always pack?
Are you travelling anywhere in the next few months? What are your plans?

lessons.title: Speaking: Get ready! Get set! Go!

2B.title: Go to checkout
words: I get fresh bread from the baker's on the corner.
The chemist's stays open until midnight.
I need to go to the chemist's.
a shop that cleans clothes without water
My coat is at the dry cleaner's.
take + noun + to the dry cleaner's
I took my suit to the dry cleaner's.
a place where you get your hair cut
She has an appointment at the hairdresser's.
I was at the hairdresser's for two hours.
a business that sells and rents homes
We found the flat through an estate agent's.
There's an estate agent's opposite the bank.
the place where you pay in a shop
There was a long queue at the checkout.
The website saves the items in your basket.
I added it to my basket.
Delivery is free on orders over fifty dollars.
a paper that shows what you paid
Keep the receipt in case you need to return it.
The shop gave me a full refund.
I asked for a full refund.
The shoes aren't in stock in my size.
The phone is out of stock.
Students get a ten per cent discount.
There's a twenty per cent discount today.

g.title: Possessives
g.rule:
Show who something belongs to.

person + 'sAnna's bag · my parents' car
shops and homesI'm going to the chemist's. · We met at Tom's.
of for thingsthe end of the street · the price of bread
a friend of mineShe's a friend of mine. · It was an idea of his.

ex.q: I bought it at the ___.
What's the name ___?
He's a colleague of ___ (I).

talk: Which local shops do you use, and which things do you buy online?
Describe your best or worst experience of shopping online.

3A.title: Grow up!
words: a very young child who is learning to walk
When she was a toddler, she used to hide under the table.
As a toddler, he never slept.
the time when you are a child
I spent my childhood in a small village.
a person aged thirteen to nineteen
As a teenager, I used to argue with my parents.
As a teenager, she loved music.
a person who is fully grown
He became an adult very young.
в возрасте двадцати с лишним лет
She was living abroad in her twenties.
He got married in his thirties.
about forty to sixty years old
A middle-aged man was waiting outside.
no longer working because of age
My grandparents are retired and travel a lot.
change from a child to an adult
She grew up in the country.
look after a child until it is an adult
She was brought up by her grandmother.
He was brought up by his aunt.
We weren't allowed to watch TV on school nights.
I was allowed to stay up late.
My parents were quite strict about homework.
did regularly in the past, but not now
I used to walk to school every day.
We used to live near the sea.

g.title: Past simple, past continuous, or used to?
g.rule:
Three ways to talk about the past.

a finished action → past simpleI left school in 2015.
an action in progress → past continuousI was living with my parents when I met her.
a past habit or state → used toI used to play outside every day. · We didn't use to have a car.

ex.q: When I was a child, we ___ every summer at my grandmother's.
I ___ home when I saw the accident.
Did you ___ (use to) wear a uniform?

talk: What did you use to do as a child that you don't do now?
Were your parents strict? What were you allowed to do?

lessons.title: Past simple, past continuous, or used to?

3B.title: Photo albums
words: a book or collection of photos
We keep our wedding photos in an album.
She showed me her photo album.
a photo or painting of a person
There's a portrait of my grandmother on the wall.
He took a portrait of his son.
a photo or painting of the countryside
He takes beautiful landscapes of the steppe.
at the back of a picture
You can see the mountains in the background.
There's a river in the background.
at the front of a picture
The children are in the foreground.
There's a dog in the foreground.
My mother is in the middle of the photo.
He's in the middle of the group.
The woman on the left is my aunt.
The man on the right is my uncle.
My father is standing behind me.
The house is behind the trees.
The photo is out of focus, but I love it.
Half the photos are out of focus.
Zoom in and you can see her face.
make a picture with a camera
Could you take a photo of us?
I took a photo of the lake.
I rarely print my photos these days.

g.title: Prepositions
g.rule:
Small words with fixed uses.

placein the photo · on the left · at the back · behind the tree
movementwalk along the beach · go through the gate · jump into the water
after adjectives and verbsgood at · interested in · depend on · think about

ex.q: There are mountains ___ the background.
She's really good ___ taking portraits.
My brother is standing ___ the left.

talk: Describe a favourite photo: who is in it, and where are they?
Do you print your photos or leave them on your phone? Why?

4A.title: Don't throw it away!
words: things you don't want any more
Who's going to take the rubbish out?
We're going to recycle more this year.
The bin is full; I'll empty it.
the box or plastic round a product
There's too much plastic packaging on food.
I try to avoid plastic packaging.
use more of something than you need
Shall we try not to waste so much food?
I won't throw it away; I'll repair it.
I'm going to reuse these jars.
a place where rubbish is buried
Most of our rubbish will end up in landfill.
Old clothes end up in landfill.
I'll look for a second-hand bike.
food that remains after a meal
We'll have the leftovers for lunch tomorrow.
Shall I take out the recycling?
Recycling is going to help the environment.

g.title: Future forms: will / shall and be going to
g.rule:
Choose the form by the kind of future.

a plan → be going toI'm going to recycle more this year.
a decision now, an offer, a promise → willThe bin is full. I'll empty it.
a suggestion or offer → shallShall I take the rubbish out? · Shall we repair it?
a predictionPrices will rise. · Look, it's going to fall.

ex.q: ___ I help you carry those bags?
I've decided. I ___ buy a second-hand bike.
Don't worry, I ___ (not / throw) it away.

talk: What are you going to do to waste less this year?
Do you think people will recycle more in the future? Why or why not?

lessons.title: Future forms: will / shall and be going to

4B.title: Put it on your CV
words: If I had a degree, I would earn more.
She has a degree in economics.
You'll need a qualification if you want this job.
He has a qualification in nursing.
a short period of work to get experience
If I do an internship, I'll learn a lot.
She did an internship at a bank.
a period of learning a job while working
He did an apprenticeship as an electrician.
I'd like to do an apprenticeship.
a job for only part of the week
If I had a part-time job, I'd have more money.
Many students have a part-time job.
If you have experience, you'll get an interview.
an ability to do something well
Speaking English is a useful skill.
ask for a job in writing
If I were you, I'd apply for the job.
apply for + a job / a course
go to an event or a course
If you attend every class, you'll pass.
When I graduate, I'll look for work abroad.
I'd stay if they offered me a permanent job.
the latest time to finish something
If we miss the deadline, we won't get paid.

g.title: First and second conditionals
g.rule:
Is the situation possible or only imagined?

possible → if + present, willIf you apply now, you'll get an interview.
imagined → if + past, wouldIf I had a degree, I'd earn more.
adviceIf I were you, I'd do an internship.
unlessYou won't pass unless you attend the classes.

ex.q: If I ___ more experience, I'd apply for that job.
If you miss the deadline, you ___ the job.
If I ___ (be) you, I'd take the course.

talk: What would you study if you could start again?
What will you do if you get the chance to work abroad?

lessons.title: Speaking: Put it on your CV

5A.title: Screen time
words: a set of TV programmes with the same story
I've watched the whole series in one weekend.
I've just seen the last episode.
The first episode is the best.
a group of episodes shown in one year
I've seen a brilliant documentary about bees.
It's a documentary about the sea.
Have you seen the news tonight?
I watch the news every evening.
a person who introduces a programme
The presenter has worked there for years.
a device for controlling the TV
I've lost the remote control again.
watch a programme on the internet
We've started streaming films at home.
I've binge-watched three seasons this week.
words on the screen that show what is said
I've always watched films with subtitles.
I watch it with English subtitles.

g.title: Present perfect simple
g.rule:
Use it to link the past with now.

experienceI've seen every episode. · Have you ever watched it?
just / already / yetI've just finished it. · They've already made five seasons. · I haven't seen it yet.
an unfinished periodI've watched two films this week.
finished time → past simpleI watched it last night.

ex.q: I ___ that documentary last week.
Have you watched the final episode ___?
She has just ___ (start) a new series.

talk: What is the best series you have ever watched? Why?
How have your TV habits changed in the last five years?

5B.title: A quiet life?
words: an area of land for crops or animals
We've been walking across fields all morning.
There are cows in the field.
land and buildings for crops or animals
They've been running the farm for thirty years.
The village lies in a green valley.
The children have been playing in the stream.
We drank from a mountain stream.
We've been following this path for an hour.
Follow the path to the lake.
a line of bushes round a field
A tall hedge separates the two gardens.
There's a tall hedge round the house.
The hay is kept in the old barn.
The animals sleep in a barn.
He's been looking after cattle since he was a boy.
It's been so peaceful since we moved here.
The farm is isolated, and I've been feeling lonely.
They live in an isolated house.
I've been commuting to the city for two years.
a person who lives near you
Our nearest neighbour lives two kilometres away.
The nearest neighbour is a farmer.

g.title: Present perfect continuous
g.rule:
Use have been + -ing for an activity that started in the past and continues, or has just stopped.

how longWe've been living here for two years / since 2023.
a recent activity with a resultI'm tired. I've been working on the farm.
non-action verbs → simpleWe've known our neighbours for years.

ex.q: How long ___ in the country?
I ___ my neighbour for ten years.
They ___ (commute) to the city since March.

talk: Would you rather live in the country or in a city? Why?
What have you been doing recently to relax?
